skill.name: defuddle
skill.description: Extract clean markdown content from web pages using Defuddle CLI, removing clutter and navigation to save tokens. Use instead of WebFetch when the user provides a URL to read or analyze, for online documentation, articles, blog posts, or any standard web page.
skill.summary: Extract cleaner Markdown from web pages with Defuddle CLI to reduce clutter and token use.
skill.author: kepano

security_audit.summary: The skill is a short Defuddle CLI usage guide with no prompt injection text or hidden behavioral instructions found. Several static hits are Markdown formatting false positives, but the npm install command and Defuddle parse examples are real external command use.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the Defuddle package version or document a trusted installation source before recommending global installation.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution on user-supplied URLs
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to confirm command execution and quote URLs before running Defuddle commands.

remediation.issue: File output command can write to the workspace
remediation.suggestion: Recommend explicit output paths and user confirmation before saving extracted content to a file.

content.value_statement: Web pages often include navigation, ads, and layout text that waste tokens. This skill uses Defuddle CLI to extract cleaner Markdown for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Extracts readable Markdown from a supplied web page URL.
Removes common page clutter such as navigation, ads, and layout content.
Saves extracted Markdown to a file when requested.
Reads specific metadata fields such as title, description, and domain.
Documents output format choices for Markdown, JSON, HTML, and metadata.
limitations: Requires the Defuddle CLI to be installed before use.
Depends on the target page being reachable from the local environment.
May not handle authenticated, scripted, or blocked pages correctly.
Does not verify the accuracy of extracted page content.

use_cases.title: Review technical documentation
use_cases.description: Extract clean Markdown from online docs before asking an assistant to summarize APIs or migration steps.

use_cases.title: Collect article text for research
use_cases.description: Convert web articles into cleaner reading material with fewer navigation and advertising tokens.

use_cases.title: Prepare source material for notes
use_cases.description: Save readable Markdown from a page so it can be reviewed, cited, or added to a notes workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Extract one page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Defuddle to extract clean Markdown from this URL, then give me the main points.

prompt_templates.title: Save source material
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract this page as Markdown with Defuddle and save it to a clearly named file in the workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Read page metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Defuddle to get the title, description, and domain for this page before summarizing it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare multiple sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract clean Markdown from these URLs, then compare the claims and note any conflicts between sources.

output_examples.input: A documentation page URL with navigation, sidebar links, and footer content.
output_examples.output: Clean Markdown with the document title, headings, main body text, and fewer navigation tokens.

output_examples.input: A blog post URL that includes ads, sharing widgets, and related article links.
output_examples.output: Readable article text focused on the post content, with clutter removed before summarization.

output_examples.input: A page URL where only metadata is needed.
output_examples.output: The page title, description, or domain value requested for quick source review.

best_practices: Confirm the URL and command before running Defuddle on user-provided input.
Prefer Markdown output for summaries, analysis, and documentation workflows.
Use explicit file names when saving extracted content to the workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for pages that require private authentication without user approval.
Do not assume extracted content is complete when the page depends on heavy scripting.
Do not save output over existing files without checking the target path.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant to use Defuddle CLI to extract cleaner Markdown from web pages.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need installation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects the Defuddle CLI to be installed before extraction commands run.

faq.question: Can it save extracted content?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a documented pattern for saving Markdown output to a file.

faq.question: Can it extract metadata?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents title, description, and domain metadata extraction.

faq.question: Is it safe to use on any URL?
faq.answer: Use care with untrusted URLs and confirm command execution before running local CLI commands.
